resources.title: Make the renewal conversation count
resources.summary: Review what has changed, organize the questions, and leave the client with a clear next step.
resources.bodyHtml:
Start with the changes

Confirm household members, drivers, vehicles, property use and contact preferences. Ask about changes since the last review before recommending a next step.

Bring the right documents

  • Review the current policy and renewal documents together.
  • Record questions about limits, deductibles and named insureds.
  • Use the policy documents to explain the terms that apply.
  • Capture the client's preferred follow-up date and owner.

Close the loop

Save a concise follow-up with the outstanding question and the next action. A saved follow-up does not change a policy.

resources.title: Build a stronger BOP submission
resources.summary: Gather the business story and property details before beginning your request.
resources.bodyHtml:
Begin with the business

A businessowners policy brings property and general liability coverages together. Workers compensation and commercial auto should be considered separately; review the applicable policy terms and underwriting guidance.

Prepare the account

  • Confirm the legal name, ownership and risk locations.
  • Describe the operations in plain language, including services, customers and changes.
  • Gather property details, annual sales, payroll and prior coverage information as requested.
  • Identify unanswered questions before submitting for review.

Choose a clear next step

Use the appetite finder for the selected state and business type, then prepare the request. Submission is a request for review and does not bind coverage.

resources.title: Start the business-vehicle conversation
resources.summary: Clarify how vehicles are owned, used and driven before preparing a commercial auto request.
resources.bodyHtml:
Understand the operation

  • Identify owned, leased and hired vehicles.
  • Describe business use, operating radius and garaging locations.
  • Confirm who drives and what driver information is requested.
  • Ask about deliveries, equipment and changes expected during the term.

Use these questions to organize the conversation. Coverage recommendations and requirements depend on the actual operation, policy and underwriting review.

resources.title: Workers compensation: a Texas starting point
resources.summary: A source-linked overview for discussions with Texas employers.
resources.bodyHtml:
Begin with the employer and the work

Texas does not require workers compensation coverage for most private employers. Private employers contracting with government entities must provide coverage for employees working on the project. Contracts may also require subcontractors or independent contractors to carry coverage.

Check the source before advising

Coverage choices have consequences beyond the premium. Review the Texas Department of Insurance guide for the employer's situation, including obligations that may apply when an employer does not provide workers compensation.

This is an educational starting point. It does not determine legal obligations or Liberty Mutual underwriting eligibility.

Read the Texas Department of Insurance guide

resources.title: Workers compensation: a Florida starting point
resources.summary: Review industry, headcount and business structure before discussing requirements.
resources.bodyHtml:
Industry and entity structure matter

Florida requirements vary by industry, employee count and entity organization. Construction employers generally need coverage with one or more employees; non-construction employers generally need coverage with four or more. Agricultural employers have separate thresholds.

Review the details

Owner treatment, exemptions, out-of-state work and contractor obligations need careful review. Use the Florida Department of Financial Services guidance to check the full requirements for the employer's circumstances.

This educational summary does not replace the official guidance or determine Liberty Mutual underwriting eligibility.

Read Florida coverage requirements

resources.title: Workers compensation: an Illinois starting point
resources.summary: Know when to review coverage with an Illinois employer.
resources.bodyHtml:
Review coverage from the first employee

The Illinois Workers' Compensation Commission explains that an employer with one employee, including a part-time employee, generally must obtain workers compensation insurance. Rare statutory exceptions apply.

Keep the circumstances in view

Entity owners may have particular opt-out provisions, and some extra-hazardous occupations require further review. Consult the Commission's insurance guidance and the applicable law rather than assuming that an ownership title creates an exemption.

This is educational content and does not determine an employer's legal obligations or Liberty Mutual underwriting eligibility.

Read Illinois insurance guidance

resources.title: Prepare the farm account story
resources.summary: Bring property, operations and seasonal activity into one organized referral.
resources.bodyHtml:
Describe the whole operation

Begin with the people, locations and activities. Note seasonal changes, related businesses and work performed away from the main property.

  • Organize locations and building use.
  • Summarize equipment, vehicles and storage.
  • Describe employees, contractors and visitor activity.
  • List existing policies and questions for the specialist.

Send a focused referral with the missing information identified. These preparation steps are a conversation framework, not a statement of product availability.

resources.title: Keep a complex renewal moving
resources.summary: Give every location, requirement and question a clear owner.
resources.bodyHtml:
Build one reliable account view

Confirm the location schedule, business activities and changes since the last review. Use consistent names and dates across the package.

  • Reconcile the location schedule with the account overview.
  • Assign each outstanding requirement.
  • Summarize material changes in a short cover note.
  • Separate coverage questions from missing-document tasks.
  • Agree the next review milestone with the account team.

Keep specialist questions connected to the case so the next person can continue the work with context.

resources.title: Turn a complex need into a focused referral
resources.summary: Help the specialist understand the risk, the question and the intended next step.
resources.bodyHtml:
Lead with the question

State the client's concern and the operation involved. Identify the parties, relevant jurisdictions and timing before attaching supporting information.

  • Describe the exposure in the client's language.
  • Identify existing coverage and the unresolved question.
  • Gather only the information required for the referral.
  • Confirm the appropriate distribution path and specialist.

A referral begins a review. It is not a coverage determination or a commitment to place the risk.

resources.title: Prepare a clear bond request
resources.summary: Organize the principal, obligee and obligation before sending the request for review.
resources.bodyHtml:
Use the right parties and terms

  • Confirm the principal's legal name.
  • Identify the obligee and the underlying obligation.
  • Record the requested bond type, amount and required date.
  • Include the required form and supporting documents.
  • Make any rider, consent or renewal request explicit.

Keep questions and requirements together in the request timeline. A submitted request is pending review and does not issue a bond.

resources.title: Create a useful wholesale handoff
resources.summary: Preserve the retail partner's context while keeping the placement path clear.
resources.bodyHtml:
Connect the parties

Record the retail agency, wholesale broker, client and specialist roles clearly. Confirm who owns communication at the next step.

  • Summarize the risk and requested consideration.
  • Confirm the jurisdictions and proposed timing.
  • Record the supporting information already provided.
  • List open questions and the next responsible party.

Follow the appropriate licensed distribution path. Do not present a placement status as evidence of coverage.

resources.title: Expand your small-business practice
resources.summary: Build confidence in the conversation, then prepare your next submission.
resources.bodyHtml:
Start with what you know

Your client relationships can help you understand how a business operates. Begin with discovery, then bring the right information to the commercial conversation.

A practical three-step path

  1. Understand the business. Review common BOP considerations and the role of workers compensation and commercial auto.
  2. Check the context. Explore guidance for the risk state and business type.
  3. Prepare the request. Use the submission checklist and ask your relationship team about unresolved questions.

Choose one next action for your agency: complete the learning path, review a resource with a teammate, or prepare an appetite inquiry.
